✅ "Once you see it, you can't unsee it"

✗ "It is recommended that the player..."
✗ "Users should ensure that..."
✗ "The following section will detail..."
✗ "One must consider..."

**Pro Tips (use > blockquotes for standout advice):**
> 💡 **Pro tip:** The audio cue is your best friend—listen for the sword whoosh before parrying.

> ⚠️ **Watch out:** His shield steal activates on YOUR turn start, so time buffs carefully.



WRITING PRINCIPLES:
You are writing a game guide section that helps players succeed. Your output should be:

• CLEAR: Players know exactly what to do next
• ACCURATE: Every specific detail comes from the research provided
• HELPFUL: Focus on practical information players need
• NATURAL: Write like a knowledgeable human sharing tips, not a robot following templates

TONE AND STRUCTURE:
• Use second person ("you") with an instructional, helpful tone
• Be specific with numbers, steps, and item names: "equip the Fire Sword" not "equip a weapon"
• Use sequential language when appropriate: "First," "Next," "After that," "Finally"
• Anticipate common mistakes: "Be careful not to miss..."
• Keep paragraphs focused (3-5 sentences) and end sections with actionable takeaways
• Write naturally—vary your sentence structure and avoid repetitive patterns



PRECISION REQUIREMENTS:

**1. Name Things Immediately**
When introducing anything with a proper name, lead with the name:
✅ "the **Shadow Temple**, the fourth dungeon in the region"
✅ "**Commander Vance**, leader of the Royal Guard, directs you to the fortress"
✅ "**Thornwood Village**, a fortified settlement south of the capital"

Not like this:
"the fourth dungeon in the region, known as the Shadow Temple" (name arrives too late)

• If it says "Room of Awakening" → write "Room of Awakening" (not "awakening chamber" or "before the cave exit")

Only include specific details that appear in your research. Never invent:
• UI elements (icon colors, menu layouts, map markers)

### Unlocking Your First Abilities

Your adventure starts here—the **Great Sky Island** stretches before you, and your first goal is acquiring the abilities that'll carry you through the entire game.

Head to the **Ukouh Shrine** on the island's western side, near the **Temple of Time**. Inside, you'll unlock **Ultrahand**, your first Zonai ability. Press **[L]** to activate and **[A]** to attach objects together—this is the foundation of almost every puzzle you'll face.

> 💡 **Pro tip:** Spend a few minutes just playing with Ultrahand here. The physics are forgiving, and experimenting now saves frustration later.

After the shrine, explore the temple's lower caverns to find the **Room of Awakening**. Grab the **Archaic Legwear** from the chest for basic defense, and don't miss the **Old Wooden Shield** leaning against the wall near the exit—shields are your lifeline in early combat.

    Simon the Divergent Star is an optional, enhanced version of the original Simon boss found in The Abyss. Located within the Endless Tower, this boss serves as a high-level challenge for players who have mastered the game's parry and build systems. He is found by heading past the gauntlet canvas to the upper platform and entering a giant Canvas. Simon has no elemental weaknesses or resistances and lacks a traditional weak spot, making the fight a pure test of endurance and mechanical skill. The encounter is divided into two distinct phases, with a forced party wipe and full boss heal occurring at the transition, necessitating at least two well-rounded expedition teams.

Phase 1 begins with a mandatory opening move called 'Multi-Sweep Slash,' where Simon attacks 9 times at light speed. This move ignores player speed and turn order pictos. Players must watch the pillars of light (White, Green, Red, Yellow) behind Simon to determine the rhythm of afterimage strikes. The final strike of this combo is critical; failing to parry or dodge it results in the current party being removed from the canvas permanently. Simon also utilizes 'Shield Steal' to siphon all player shields, 'Chroma Stack' to reduce an expeditioner to 1 HP, and 'Anti-Revive' to permanently remove fallen members from the fight. His 'Pillar Slash' combos can reach up to 24 strikes in the 'long' variant or 12 in the 'powerful' variant, with the rhythm dictated by the color and spacing of the light pillars.

Upon reaching low health, Simon triggers Phase 2 with 'Canvas Removal,' stomping the ground to eliminate the first team and healing himself to 100% HP. The second team must then take over. In this phase, he gains the 'Lumiere Strike,' a spinning attack that culminates in a beam of light and a final sword strike. This final hit is lethal, bypassing 'Second Chance' and Simoso’s level 20 invincibility perk. A key warning for both phases is to avoid breaking Simon; if stunned, he becomes invulnerable to all damage until his next turn, effectively wasting player resources.

Strategic advice from the community suggests using a high-speed Verso (3300-3600+ speed) for Phase 1, utilizing 'Simoso' and 'Cheater' to maintain S-rank and immortality. For Phase 2, a combination of Sciel, Maelle, and Lune is recommended. Sciel can use 'Delaying Slash' to push Simon back in the turn order, while Maelle acts as the primary damage dealer using 'Virtuoso Stance' and 'Esqium' to deal upwards of 20,000,000 damage per turn. Players are encouraged to equip 'Cheater,' 'Clea’s Life,' and 'Second Chance' on all members to survive the encounter's high damage output.

Defeating Simon rewards the player with unique 'Simon Haircut' cosmetics for Lune, Sciel, Maelle, Monoco, and Verso. Additionally, players receive 20x Colour of Lumina, 5x Grandiose Chroma Catalyst, and 1x Perfect Chroma Catalyst. The experience reward is a massive 24,750,000 XP, which increases to 29,700,000 XP if the player completes the battle without taking any damage. On higher New Game+ cycles, such as NG+5, Simon's total health pool can reach approximately 600 million HP.

As this is the hardest encounter in the game, it may seem obvious to properly plan which members of your party are active going into the fight. But Simon presents a unique challenge that no other enemy in the game can employ. If you wish to remain spoiler-free on a mechanic in the fight, skip over the spoiler-flagged section below:

In Phase 2 of the fight, when you get Simon's health to around 30-40%, he will immediately perform a move that erases all active party members from the canvas. This is different to him removing dead party members from the canvas throughout the fight, as all members (alive or dead) are immediately gone. And you can't do anything about it.

Whether you've read the spoilers above or not, here's a tip: **Do not go in with a full party of 3 active members**. It's also a good call to **go into the fight with the weakest members of your party**, and keeping the stronger characters in reserve.

## Parry, Parry, and More Parries

This is honestly the one thing that may trip many players up dependent on your skill level and how consistent you are with your parry timing. As the fight progresses, the importance of perfecting every single parry becomes far more important. Simon packs a hefty punch with his attacks normally, but the combos he can perform in Phase 2 and beyond can (and will) essentially one-shot you. Here's what parrying will look like in each phase of the fight:

### Phase 1

In Phase 1 with his first health bar, the attacks are relatively telegraphed and aren't coming too fast.

**As his health dips below 50%, he can perform a longer combo of sword swipes** but again they come relatively slowly and predictably (at least in comparison to what's to come).

### Phase 2

After fully depleting his first health bar, Simon will now essentially have two swords - one ethereal blade following behind his actual sword. This means that all the attacks from Phase 1 that required one parry per slash will now require two consecutive parries. What results from this is that at points you'll be pressing parry non-stop for 5-10 seconds, especially with the "long attack".

You'll also have the "speed of light" and "Sword of Lumiere" attacks, with the Speed of Light being particularly deadly just due to how quickly the slashes come in. A good tip for the "speed of light" attack is that it consists of **10 total attacks** you'll need to parry.

There will be **7 consecutive slashes** back and forth, and then there will be a **brief pause after the 7th and before the 8th slash**, so don't keep spamming parry - count out the attacks if it helps!

The section below will spoil a unique mechanic for the fight (described in the spoiler section above), so read on with caution if you don't want to be spoiled before experiencing it for yourself!

### Phase 3

When you deplete his second health bar to around 40%, Simon will immediately perform an unpreventable move that erases all active party members from the canvas.

This means you'll have to call in any/all party members in Reserve. Alongside this, **a third sword is added** - meaning those two consecutive parries in Phase 2 will now become three on all attacks (outside of the "speed of light" and "Sword of Lumiere" attacks).

## Use Gradient Attacks Often

Regardless of which phase of the fight you're on, you'll really want to maximise your damage output at every opportunity. If you're able to build up to Level 3 and Gommage with Maelle whilst she's in Virtuose Stance, or Break Point with Monoco, then that's ideal. Always keep a close eye or when you can quickly stack debuffs/status effects, and pay close attention to what skills can subsequently capitalise off of them.

Greysun is the lead guides editor at Game Rant, covering all the biggest AAA titles to the smaller indie gems. He's been a big Nintendo fan since the SNES days and patiently awaits a Super Mario Odyssey sequel.

If you're a Trophy (or Achievement) hunter, then you might be wondering how to get the '**Peace at Last**' achievement in ***Clair Obscur: Expedition 33***. The trophy requires players to find and defeat a character named **Simon.** This guide will show players where to find Simon and provide tips on how to beat him.

It's worth noting that this guide will go into some **spoilers for the endgame** of [*Clair Obscur: Expedition 33*](https://gamerant.com/db/video-game/clair-obscur-expedition-33/), so please proceed with caution if you're worried about finding out secrets unorganically. You should be done with the main story at this point.

## Simon Location in Clair Obscur Expedition 33

### Be Prepared

Utilize Esquie's power of swimming to head to a part of the ocean that's smack-dab in **between Sirene and Visages**. You'll find a portal that leads to a new map called **Renoir's Drafts**.

This entrance is unlike others, as there is no actual structure visible on the surface of the water - **it will simply be a portal**. You can check out the images above to get a better picture.

Once you make your way through **Renoir's Drafts** (it's not that big of a map!), you will find another portal that leads to **The Abyss**, and then you can reach Simon and face him in a battle. A very difficult **two-phase battle** as a matter of fact.

## Tips for Beating Simon in Clair Obscur: Expedition 33

Here are some important notes that should help make the fight against Simon less irritating...

* There are two phases. Once you get this initial health bar down to zero, a cutscene will happen, and then a new fight will start.
* If you die in the second phase, you will have to restart the entire battle.
* He has a move that can put any party member's health down to 1.
* He can also remove a fainted party member from the battle, which means you cannot revive them. Once this happens to one or two of your strongest party members, it might be best to just start over at that point.
* In the second phase, some of his moves will be doubled, so the moves you got used to in the first phase will need to be double-parried (you'll see what I mean once you get to the second part). And eventually, that'll increase to three.
* [Learning how to parry is a must](https://gamerant.com/clair-obscur-expedition-33-how-time-parries/), but if you must, dodge to be safe.
* We used a very powerful build for **Maelle** that involves using her [Last Chance](https://expedition33.wiki.fextralife.com/Last+Chance) skill to reduce her health to 1, but refilling her AP to use a strong move, like Stendhal, to do massive damage. **Last Chance will put her into the Virtuose Stance**, increasing her attack power. You can take advantage of the low health by equipping Pictos that give **damage boosts for having low HP in battle**, such as [At Death's Door](https://expedition33.wiki.fextralife.com/At+Death's+Door) .
* Use the [Cheater](https://expedition33.wiki.fextralife.com/Cheater) Pictos on all of your party members to give them a second turn. It costs 40 Lumina Points, but it's a total game-changer.

## Reward for Defeating Simon in Clair Obscur Expedition 33

If you manage to get through the fight, you will be rewarded with a new weapon for Verso: the [Simoso](https://expedition33.wiki.fextralife.com/Simoso). You can also **pick up Simon's Journal** nearby to get closer to unlocking the Follow the Trail achievement. You can read it if you want some more lore about the wild story of *Clair Obscur*.

### Observe the Pillars of Light

The pillars of light behind Simon before they attack indicates the **number of follow-ups** and the **timing of their appearance** in their attack. The **white light** refers to the **sword**, while the **cyan**, **red**, and **yellow** lights are the **follow-ups**.

The follow-ups are **in order from left to right**. If only the white and red pillars appear, then the attack will only have the 2nd follow-up, skipping the 1st follow-up from the cyan light.

### Dodge or Parry the Last Hit of the Light Speed Attack

Simon, The Divergent will always play first to cast the **light speed attack**, bypassing [First Strike](/games/Clair-Obscur-Expedition-33/archives/517433) and the [Auto Death](/games/Clair-Obscur-Expedition-33/archives/517491), [Second Chance](/games/Clair-Obscur-Expedition-33/archives/517967), [Revive Paradox](/games/Clair-Obscur-Expedition-33/archives/519144) combo.

It is imperative to at least **dodge** or **parry** the final hit of the combo, as it forcibly removes the party when it connects, bypassing revives from **Second Chance** and [Verso](/games/Clair-Obscur-Expedition-33/archives/516112)'s **Aureole**.

    Simon The Divergent Star is a high-level optional boss introduced in the Thank You Update for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Located within the Endless Tower in Act 3, this encounter is designed for players at Level 99.
